It only looked right because pressing = between steps works, and that is how every scenario before this one was written. trigOperand() had been folding the whole run correctly the entire time, so two evaluators disagreed about the same tape. The fold is left to right with no precedence — 2 + 3 × 4 is 20 — which is what Construction Master Pro and BuildCalc do, and the only order the tape can be read in: each chip applies to the running total on its left. A trig chip has a key and an angle has no unit, so it failed both and the edit was treated as permanently mid-keystroke: the results below it dashed out and never came back. Rev 8 opened that surface by keeping Sine 89° on the tape as a chip with digits in it, where Sine 0.999848 had nothing to tap. An angle is complete WITHOUT a unit; that is what makes it an angle. Separately, a failed rebuild used to run state.editInPlace = null while the chip stayed active and kept taking digits — and render() only recomputes while editInPlace is set, so every keystroke after a failure edited the tape with nothing recomputing, and the screen could read 70 ÷ 89 = 0.079 wearing the green just-recomputed glow, then seal it. scenarios.name: Tapping a closed ( ) chip reopens the group, and the chip stays one chip the whole time
scenarios.keys: A user tapped the blue chip "+(3×4)" and nothing seemed to happen. The chip used to edit only the folded number 12, in a style that looked the same before and after the tap, and typing one digit turned it into a plain number. The first attempt at a fix broke the chip back into separate chips, 3 and ×4, on the tape. The user rejected that: "I don't want to break them into individual chips, that feels like so breaking experience." So a tap now only removes the closing bracket. The chip stays exactly where it is, reading "+(3×4", live, and the keypad types inside it
scenarios.expected: One tap and the chip reads "+(3×4" — the same single chip, minus its closing bracket, on the live green. The tape still holds exactly two chips, so nothing has been taken apart. Backspace, 5 and ) rewrite it to "+(3×5" then "+(3×5)", and the answer follows: 2 + 15 reads 17

scenarios.name: Reopening a group in the middle of a calculation recomputes everything after it

The answer keeps its chip but shows a dash instead of 70, because a reviewer pointed out that a faded 70 was the one number on screen that looked like a finished answer and was wrong. Closing the group wakes them again and the same in-place recompute used for a tapped number rebuilds the answer

scenarios.keys: Closing (3×4) put 12 in the big number while the chip still read +(3×4). The two drawings of one chip disagreed, and 12 read like a wrong answer to 2+(3×4). The big number is never the running total in this app. It is the number you are working on. The small line above it already names how that number is being read, so it names the group too
